reaches_users:
Nothing I found is new in 1.7.0, and 1.7.0 reaches nobody on native yet — so almost every item here is already in front of all ~500 downloads.

- **Streak silent on day 1** — the `result.streak > 1` gate dates to commit 8f08eb9, 2026-05-01. Live on web at HEAD, live on iOS 1.6.0, live on Play vc20. Every player who has ever finished their first puzzle has hit it.
- **Milestones only at 7/30/100** — same, all platforms, all builds.
- **`scores` under-recording ~20% of daily completions** — server-side, platform-independent. It is corrupting the numbers right now on every device and every dashboard.
- **Notification reach** (37 device tokens / 1 web push subscriber / 12 notifications ever) — current prod state, all platforms.
- **No server-side win-back push for native** — cron.job has 4 jobs and none of them touch device_tokens. 28 players are now past the +30-day end of the local WINBACK tail and are permanently silent.
- **Consent banner clipping the ENTER key** — **web only, and only EU/UK/CH** (public/consent.js is fetched only for European visitors). That happens to be GB and NO, our two biggest storefronts.
- **Repair-banner dead copy** — all platforms, but I could not construct a realistic user state that reaches it, so treat it as latent.

The one 1.7.0 retention change — `notif-prompt-skipped` reasons (afff13c, deployed 13:43 today) — is **web-only in effect** and has produced exactly 1 row in 7 hours, because the branch it lives in only runs when `notificationsSupported()` is false. It will stay near-silent until native builds ship.
evidence: **The cliff is not day-1→day-2. It is started→finished.** 217 accounts. 133 (61%) have ever finished a game; 84 (39%) never have. Of the 133 finishers, 94 (70.7%) came back on a second day. Of the 84 non-finishers, **0** ever did. Activity defined as scores ∪ room_players.joined_at ∪ daily_scores keys ∪ wordle_state won/lost keys.

**The brief's premise does not survive the fuller activity table.** Among everyone who ever did anything, one-and-done is 34%, not 56%; 66% returned. The 56% comes from reading `scores` alone, which misses ~20% of daily completions (below). Corrected split: 67 accounts with zero activity of any kind, 51 exactly-one-day, 34 two-day, 28 three-to-six, 37 seven-plus.

**The FIRST puzzle decides, and only the first.** By first-ever Footle outcome: won → 78.5% ever returned (n=65); lost → 58.3% (n=36); abandoned mid-board → 45.5% (n=22). Two-proportion z: won-vs-lost z≈2.15 (p≈0.03), won-vs-abandoned z≈2.29 (p≈0.02). **47% of first Footles end in a loss or an abandon.**

**Difficulty does NOT drive churn for existing players — I tested my own hypothesis and it failed.** Across 479 decided Footle sessions since 2026-07-20, next-day return was 63.6% after a LOSS and 62.9% after a WIN. Flat. Within 3 days there is a modest gap (74.4% vs 83.1%). I was one query away from recommending 'make Footle easier' to the whole base, which the data says would buy nothing.

**`scores` is missing ~20% of daily completions, every day.** Today's puzzle only, so archive plays and guest back-sync are both excluded: 2026-08-23 Footle — 13 finished in user_game_state, 12 score rows; 08-22 18 vs 16; 08-21 17 vs 15; 08-20 19 vs 15; 08-19 18 vs 12; 08-18 17 vs 12. Week totals: Footle 118 vs 96, Daily 7 98 vs 77. Cross-checked per-user: 510 finished Footles in state since 2026-07-20 vs 348 footle rows in `scores` — 162 unrecorded across 68 users, 25 of whom have zero footle rows at all.

**12 accounts have a finished puzzle on the server and games_played=0, xp=0, total_score=0.** One of them has 12 finished Footles and 6 Daily-7 days recorded in user_game_state and a profile that says they have played nothing. Their leaderboard row, their level, their XP: all zero.

**Streak day 1 is silent. Verified twice, by DOM polling at 250ms over 12s.** Fresh state, won today's Footle in one guess: `biq_login_streak` = {streak:1}, and the string 'streak' and the 🔥 glyph appear **nowhere** on screen except the app-install pitch ('Streaks, daily reminders and every quiz in one app'). Seeded to streak=4 and repeated: '🔥 5 day streak! Keep it up' fires reliably for ~3.5s. src/App.jsx:8998 — `else if (result.ticked && result.streak > 1)`.

**The celebration ladder starts above where 93% of players die.** Prod streak distribution (185 users with a login_streak): best=1 → 101 users (55%), 2 → 28, 3 → 14, 4 → 12, 5 → 5, 6 → 2, 7+ → 23 (12.4%). Milestone celebrations exist at **7, 30, 100** only (src/App.jsx:9025). Days 2 and 3 — where 42 of the 84 surviving players are standing — get nothing beyond the 3.5s toast.

**The reminder machine has delivered 12 notifications in the product's lifetime.** notifications table by type: play_invite 5, friend_request 3, **daily_reminder 2**, friend_accept 1, generic 1. The hourly `web-daily-reminder` cron has one possible recipient: web_push_subscriptions holds 1 row.

**77% of lapsed players are unreachable.** 84 players have not played in 7+ days. 19 have a device token. 0 have a web push subscription. 28 are past 30 days — beyond the last WINBACK local notification (offsets 8/11/15/22/30 in src/lib/notifications.js:24) — and cron.job contains 4 jobs, none of which pushes to device_tokens. There is no server-side win-back for native, ever.

**The web notification ask is unreachable for the people actually finishing puzzles.** src/App.jsx:10183 `if (!user?.id) return bail("guest")`. Every onboard-done row in funnel_events for the last 48h is `signed_in: false, native: false` — 10 answered, 3 skipped, all guests. The only notif-prompt-skipped row in prod reads `{reason: "unsupported", engine: "web"}`, and notif-prompt-shown has never fired.

**Zero instrumentation of the loop we say is the binding constraint.** funnel_events has no event for daily-completed, streak-ticked, streak-broken, shield-used, repair-offered, reminder-scheduled or reminder-tapped. Its 18 event types are onboarding, club-quiz and share. It also only goes back to 2026-08-21 — the 180-day cleanup_funnel_events cron is not why; the instrumentation is two days old.

**The Clarity consent banner clips the ENTER key.** Measured at 375x812 on the Footle screen: ENTER spans y 607–659 full-width (l:0, w:375); the banner spans y 643–815. `document.elementFromPoint(187, 650)` returns the banner div, not the button. public/consent.js:59 `reserveSpace()` sets body padding-bottom to 172px and it does apply (body height 984 vs root 812) — it just under-reserves by 16px inside the SPA. The banner also occupies 21% of the viewport through the whole first session.
**The shield mechanic is real and used.** 28 users have consumed 34 shields. 23 users have a live streak today; max best is 56; mean best 3.56.

**`repairLoginStreak` has exactly one trigger.** grep across src/App.jsx: defined at 9173, called at 9215 only — inside the `biq:archive-completed` listener, gated on `ymd === yesterday`. When DailyScreen.jsx:313's fallback copy shows ('the repair will land with your next play'), no code path delivers it.

findings.title: 39% of accounts never finish a single game, and not one of them ever comes back
findings.why_it_matters: 84 of 217 accounts have never completed a game; their return rate is 0%. The 133 who did finish one return at 70.7%. Every retention mechanic we have built — streak, shields, repair, countdown, reminders — is aimed at players who have already crossed that line. We have been optimising the second half of a funnel whose first half loses four in ten. This also reframes the whole area: the day-1 cliff is a first-session-completion problem, not a come-back-tomorrow problem.

findings.title: The outcome of a player's FIRST Footle swings their retention by 20 points — and 47% of first Footles end badly
findings.why_it_matters: First Footle won → 78.5% return. Lost → 58.3%. Abandoned → 45.5%. Both gaps are significant (p<0.05). Crucially, this is a first-session-only effect: for established players a loss costs nothing (63.6% vs 62.9% next-day return). So the lever is not global difficulty — it is that we hand a first-time player today's puzzle cold, and prod day-level win rates swing from 38% (2026-08-09) to 100% (2026-08-08). Roughly half of all new players meet Ball IQ on a day it beats them.

findings.title: `scores` under-records ~20% of daily completions every day — so every retention number we steer by is wrong
findings.why_it_matters: Today-only, which excludes archive plays and guest back-sync: 08-23 Footle 13 finished in user_game_state vs 12 score rows; 08-19 18 vs 12; 08-18 17 vs 12. Week totals 118 vs 96 (Footle) and 98 vs 77 (Daily 7). Consequences compound: (1) the '56% never return' figure in the brief is an artifact of this gap; (2) `enqueue_web_daily_reminders` decides 'did they play today' by reading `scores`, so it will nag people who played; (3) 12 accounts have finished puzzles on the server and a profile reading games_played 0, xp 0, total_score 0 — one with 12 finished Footles. 'I played and it didn't save' is a 3-star review with a screenshot.

findings.title: The streak says nothing at all on day 1, and the next celebration is six days away
findings.why_it_matters: src/App.jsx:8998 gates the streak toast on `streak > 1`, and milestones (9025) fire at 7/30/100. In prod, 101 of 185 streak-holders (55%) never got past 1 and only 23 (12.4%) ever reached 7. The moment a habit is born — a new player's first completion — the app is silent about the one mechanic designed to bring them back; then it stays silent through days 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6, which is where 42 of the 84 survivors are standing. I verified this twice with 250ms DOM polling, after my own first pass got it wrong (see not_verified).

findings.title: After a loss we never tell the player their streak survived
findings.why_it_matters: We made the humane, correct call — a lost Footle continues the streak, unlike NYT's — and then never say so. I lost 0/6 on purpose: the screen reads 'Better luck tomorrow / The answer was Jérôme Boateng / +10 XP', with no flame and no number, while localStorage quietly went 1→2. Wordle-literate players assume a loss kills the streak. 27% of finished Footles are losses and 36 users' first-ever Footle was one (58.3% return vs 78.5% for a win). This is our single most reassuring fact and we withhold it at precisely the moment it would do the most work.

findings.title: 77% of lapsed players are unreachable, and native has no server-side win-back at all
findings.why_it_matters: 84 players are 7+ days lapsed: 19 have a device token, 0 have web push. 28 are past 30 days, which is the last offset in the on-device WINBACK array — and cron.job has four jobs, none of which sends to device_tokens. So a native player who stops opening the app runs out of scheduled nudges after 30 days and is silent forever. The whole notification system has delivered 12 notifications in the product's life, 2 of them daily reminders.

findings.title: On web, the notification ask is structurally unreachable for the people who finish puzzles
findings.why_it_matters: src/App.jsx:10183 bails with reason 'guest' when there is no user id. Every onboard-done event in prod for the last 48 hours is `signed_in: false` — the web audience finishing puzzles is guests. notif-prompt-shown has never fired on web, which is exactly why web_push_subscriptions holds one row. The new reasons channel (shipped today) is the right instinct and will keep reporting near-nothing until the gate moves or guests get a reason to sign in first.

findings.title: We have zero instrumentation of the retention loop
findings.why_it_matters: funnel_events carries 18 event types covering onboarding, club quizzes and shares. There is no daily-completed, no streak-ticked, no streak-broken, no shield-used, no repair-offered, no reminder-scheduled, no reminder-tapped, no notif-permission-granted. We cannot answer 'do reminders work?', 'does the streak cause return?', or 'what fraction of native users granted notifications?' from data. Every number in this report had to be reconstructed from jsonb blobs that exist for other reasons. That is not a sustainable way to run the metric Alex has named the binding constraint.

findings.title: The Clarity consent banner clips the bottom 16px of the ENTER key on the first game a European player ever plays
findings.why_it_matters: Measured at 375x812: ENTER occupies y 607–659 full-width, the banner y 643–815, and elementFromPoint(187,650) returns the banner. No key's centre is blocked so the keyboard still works, but the bottom third of the one control a Footle player must press repeatedly is under a compliance bar, and the banner eats 21% of the viewport for the whole first session. public/consent.js:59 already contains a `reserveSpace()` mitigation written for the club-page taster — it applies (body grows to 984px) but under-reserves by 16px inside the SPA, so it was never verified on the surface that matters most. 51 Footle boards in prod were abandoned at 0–2 guesses. Web only, EU/UK/CH only — which is GB and NO, our two biggest storefronts.

findings.title: The streak-repair banner's fallback copy promises a repair that no code path can deliver
findings.why_it_matters: DailyScreen.jsx:313 renders 'Yesterday's puzzles are all done — the repair will land with your next play' whenever `yesterdayOpen()` returns empty. But `repairLoginStreak` has exactly one call site (App.jsx:9215), inside the `biq:archive-completed` listener gated on yesterday's date. If there is no yesterday row to play, the repair never lands. I hit this state by seeding a fallen streak on a fresh install, but could not construct a realistic user who reaches it — `matchdays` starts at the player's first-ever play day, and any genuine lapse leaves a yesterday row. Latent, not live: worth fixing the copy, not worth a sprint.

five_star_path:
**Alex's brief, quoted back:** *"we are at a stage where we have more than 500 downloads now so i really want our quality bar to be set sky high"* … *"grade us on things that actually decide if people give you a 5 star or 4 star"* … *"big strides but brick by brick... methodical and follow the data."*

Here is what the data says for retention, and it is not what any of us expected.

---

**1. WHAT GETS US TO 5 STARS**

A daily-habit app earns 5 stars from the people who kept the habit, and it earns 4 (or 1) from the people who bounced and felt something was broken. We have 8 ratings across five storefronts. To get to 10+ in GB we need more people who reach day 7 — and today only 23 of 217 accounts ever have.

Three things stand between us and those reviews, in order of size:

- **Someone who finishes one game retains at 70.7%. Someone who does not retains at 0%.** 84 of 217 accounts never finished a game. That is where the stars are, and no reminder, streak or shield touches it.
- **The first puzzle is a coin-flip that decides everything.** First Footle won → 78.5% return; lost → 58.3%; abandoned → 45.5%. And prod win rates by day swing from 38% to 100%. We are letting a random Tuesday decide whether a new player ever comes back. Losing your thirtieth Footle costs nothing measurable (63.6% vs 62.9%) — losing your **first** costs twenty points.
- **"My score didn't save."** 12 accounts have finished puzzles on the server and a profile reading zero games, zero XP, level 1. That is a 1-star review with a screenshot attached, and we are manufacturing it at roughly one in five daily completions.

**2. WHAT IMPROVES THE PRODUCT NOW — the single highest-leverage change**

**Guarantee the first win.** Concretely: a first-time player's first Footle should not be today's random puzzle. Serve a curated opener (a famous, high-frequency 7-letter surname), or grant one free letter reveal on the first-ever board only, or — cheapest of all — when a first-ever Footle is lost, immediately offer yesterday's instead of ending on "Better luck tomorrow."

Why this one: it is the only lever with a measured 20-point effect, it is confined to the first session so it cannot dilute the game for the 133 people who already love it, and the veteran data proves difficulty is *not* a problem anywhere else. Converting half of the 47% of first-Footles that currently end badly is worth roughly 10 points of return rate on ~50 new accounts a month.

Three cheap things to land alongside it, in the same brick:

- **Say "day 1" out loud.** Flip `result.streak > 1` at App.jsx:8998 and add 2 and 3 to the milestone list at 9025. 55% of streak-holders never get past 1 and the app currently says nothing to any of them. This is a copy change.
- **After a loss, say the streak survived.** "🔥 Your 2-day streak is safe — turning up is the streak." We made the kind rule; we never told anyone. Losses are 27% of finished Footles.
- **Fix the `scores` gap.** Until it is fixed we are steering by a number that is a fifth wrong, and 12 real people are looking at a profile that says they have played nothing.

**3. HOW TO THINK GOING FORWARD**

*Instrument the loop before optimising it.* I had to reconstruct every number in this report out of jsonb blobs that exist for other reasons. There is no event for a completed daily, a ticked streak, a broken streak, a used shield, a tapped reminder, or a granted notification permission. Add those six events and the next report can answer "do reminders work?" instead of inferring it. Right now the honest answer is that the notification system has delivered **12 notifications in its entire life**, and we would not have known.

*Stop building pull, start building entry.* We have a genuinely good retention machine — shields (28 users have consumed one), a repair stash, a humane loss rule, a countdown, a form table, a win-back tail. It works: finishers return at 71%. The constraint moved and we did not notice, because the metric that would have told us was reading the wrong table.

*Every retention fix must name its channel.* 65 of 84 lapsed players cannot be contacted by any means we own. Web push has one subscriber and the ask is gated on being signed in, which our web audience is not. Native local reminders stop at +30 days and there is no server-side win-back. Before the next retention feature, answer: which of these 84 people receives it?

*Brick by brick, in this order:* (1) guarantee the first win; (2) day-1 and day-2 streak copy; (3) fix the `scores` write; (4) six funnel events; (5) then, and only then, argue about notifications.

The a11y half: role="switch" without aria-checked is invalid, so VoiceOver and TalkBack cannot state the switch's state at all. Root cause is one line — App.jsx:9533 setSettings(s) replaces the correctly-merged defaults with the raw stored object — and it perpetuates itself because every later write spreads the already-clobbered state.

CSS cannot reach a canvas. Results and win screens are the highest-frequency celebratory moments in the product, so a vestibular-sensitive player who has explicitly asked the OS for less motion gets the most motion the app produces, every single time they succeed.

Browser zoom does work as a fallback and the layout reflows cleanly at 200% with zero horizontal overflow (I verified the zoom genuinely applied before trusting that), but pinch-zoom is exactly the workaround the native focus-zoom lock suppresses while a field is focused. five_star_path:
WHAT GETS US TO 5 STARS. Accessibility rarely earns a 5-star review, but two things in this area actively cost stars, and both are fixable this week. First, the Settings lie. A control whose displayed state contradicts the app's behaviour is the exact shape of "buggy, doesn't do what it says" reviews — and it is worse than a plain bug because the user tried to fix their own problem, in the place we told them to, and the app ignored them. Alex's brief says the bar is sky-high now that 500+ people have downloaded; a settings screen that shows two switches wrong fails that bar on the most literal reading. Fix App.jsx:9533 to merge rather than replace, and coerce at :6514/:6523 the way :6541 already does. Second, the 2.52:1 tab bar. Nobody writes "contrast ratio 2.52" in a review; they write "hard to read" or nothing at all, and quietly churn — which is what a 56% day-one drop-off looks like from the inside. These two are roughly an hour of work and they touch every session on every platform. Beyond that, the star-earning move is different in kind: ship 1.7.0 to iOS. The h1s, the announcer, the 12 error boundaries and the Hot Streak glyphs are all sitting on web reaching nobody on the store, and the ratings engine reaches iOS for the first time in that build. An accessibility improvement that has not been uploaded is not an accessibility improvement.

WHAT IMPROVES THE PRODUCT NOW. Three things, in this order. (1) An in-app text size control. It is the single highest-value inclusivity feature missing, because iOS Dynamic Type provably cannot reach us — 299 px declarations, zero rem — and quiz text read under a 20-second clock is precisely where small type hurts. A --scale multiplier on a :root font-size with a three-position setting would do it; the 200% zoom test already proves the layouts reflow without breaking, so the risk is low and pre-measured. (2) Gate the confetti and count-ups on matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'). Four call sites, one shared helper, and it closes the gap between what the CSS killswitch promises and what canvas actually does. (3) Surface the colour-blind toggle where the colour is. It is real, it works, and the simulation confirms it moves Footle onto the blue–yellow axis deuteranopes retain — but it is off by default and buried in Settings, so the people who need it never learn it exists. One line in Footle's how-to-play, next to the "Green = right spot" legend that is itself the giveaway, would do more than the feature has done in three days.

HOW WE SHOULD THINK GOING FORWARD. Two lessons, both earned this session. First: the coercion asymmetry at App.jsx:6514 vs :6541 is the real story, not the bug. Two switches were written defensively and two were not, in the same file, in adjacent lines. That is not a knowledge problem, it is the absence of an invariant — and the memory note about second-pass fixes getting clobbered describes this exact shape. The durable fix is not patching two toggles; it is making SettingsToggle refuse a non-boolean `val`, so the next setting cannot be added wrong. Prefer making the defect structurally impossible over fixing the instance. Second, on measurement: I produced seven wrong findings before producing nine right ones. Every wrong one died the same way — a second route disagreed with the first. The naive contrast metric even told me the colour-blind palette was WORSE than the default (1.04 vs 1.63) because luminance is the wrong axis for deuteranopia entirely. So the standing rule for accessibility specifically: never grade a colour or a tap target from CSS alone, because compositing, opacity and paint order all live between the stylesheet and the pixel — measure at the pixel, then explain the number from the source. And the one thing no amount of this method can substitute for: turn VoiceOver on, on a real iPhone, and try to play one round of Footle. Everything I report about screen readers is read from the accessibility tree, not heard.

findings.title: The first screen a new web user sees is a perfect fake: painted at 0.6s, dead until 2.9s, and it eats their first tap
findings.why_it_matters: This is report #3's 'empty frame' lesson recurring in a worse form. The pre-boot shell in index.html is sophisticated engineering — it steals LCP back from JS by painting the exact onboarding frame from static HTML — but its four answer buttons are inert markup. On production I tapped the correct answer at 1,691ms and nothing happened, ever. The user's very first interaction with Ball IQ is swallowed. There is no pressed state, no spinner, no disabled styling — nothing tells them to wait, and the screen is a pixel-perfect copy of the live one, so the only available conclusion is 'this app is broken'. It scales exactly inversely with how good your phone is: 63ms on a dev machine, 2.4 seconds on a mid-tier phone on slow 4G. That is why it survived every previous audit. 56% never return after day 1, and this is the single screen they all see first.

findings.title: Native cold launch shows ~1.0 second of pure black between the launch storyboard and the splash
findings.why_it_matters: Reproduced three times (two cold, one warm) on an iPhone 17 simulator running the actual 1.7.0 build 75: the launch storyboard shows the flaming-ball splash at ~0.45s, then the screen goes COMPLETELY BLACK from 0.81s to 1.79s, then the splash comes back, then Home appears at 3.38s. A simulator on Apple Silicon is a floor — a real iPhone, especially an older one or a first launch after install, will be worse. This is the platform where all 500+ downloads and all 8 App Store ratings live. A black screen mid-launch is the single most reliable way to make a free app feel like a cheap one, and 'slow to open' is a 4-star review that never mentions the questions. The native splash *dismissal* is beautifully handled (launchAutoHide:false, hidden only when React is ready, App.jsx:12762+); it is the *arrival* that is broken.

findings.title: 26.5KB gzipped of question-conflict map rides the boot-critical chunk for a feature that needs a different 690KB chunk to run
findings.why_it_matters: src/App.jsx:21 statically imports questionConflicts.js (78.5KB raw / 26.5KB gz), so the league answer-leak guard shipped since report #3 — a genuinely good content fix — put its entire lookup table on the critical path of every cold start for every user, including someone who only ever plays Footle. It is 11% of the compressed weight of GameRoot, the one chunk that gates React mounting, which is the exact chunk that defines the dead-tap window above. Moving it behind the same dynamic import as the question bank costs nothing in behaviour and shortens the window for everyone.

findings.title: ~1.5MB over the wire on every cold web start, of which the biggest single item is a question bank most sessions never open
findings.why_it_matters: The service worker precaches all 34 assets — 6.69MB raw / 1.75MB gzipped — starting at window load, and separately App.jsx:9469 idle-prefetches the 690KB-gzipped question bank at ~7.6s. Both are deliberate and well-argued in the code comments, and both make mode entry excellent (Footle 76ms, Trail 469ms). But they are paid by every visitor on every first visit regardless of intent, on a metered connection, in markets where we hold ratings (IN, ZA). Nobody is measuring whether that trade is winning, because CrUX has no data for balliq.app and the funnel_events mode mix is polluted by 892 robot rows from a single user.

five_star_path:
WHAT GETS US TO 5 STARS. Nobody has ever written a 5-star review of a quiz app because it scrolled at 60fps — and Ball IQ already does, with zero dropped frames at 4x CPU throttle. Stars are lost in two moments, and this area owns both. (1) The launch. A native user's first second is a black screen; that is the moment they decide whether this is a real app or a hobby project, and we are answering wrong before a single question loads. Close the ~1.0s gap between the launch storyboard and the Capacitor splash so the flaming ball is continuous from tap to Home. (2) The first tap. On web, a new visitor's very first interaction is silently eaten for up to 2.5 seconds by a screen that looks completely alive. Fix it two ways, both cheap: give the pre-boot shell's buttons a pressed state so a tap is acknowledged, and record which option was tapped into a variable that OnboardingScreen replays on mount — the swap is already pixel-identical, so a replayed tap would look instantaneous rather than ignored. Do those two things and the product stops contradicting itself in the only two seconds a reviewer is paying full attention.

WHAT IMPROVES THE CURRENT PRODUCT NOW. Everything downstream of the first frame is already good and I have the numbers: tab switches 58–136ms with no network, typing 16–59ms with a working suggestion dropdown, Trail playable 469ms after the tap with a real "Loading Transfer Trail…" state, Daily 7 on native in under 180ms with a 2.24MB bank parsed off local disk, total blocking time 54ms across a 16-second cold boot. Do not go looking for slow code — there isn't any. Go after bytes on the critical path instead, because bytes are what set the dead-tap window: move questionConflicts.js (src/App.jsx:21) behind the question-bank dynamic import and 26.5KB gzipped — 11% of the boot chunk — leaves the critical path with no behaviour change at all. Then ask the harder question about the 1.75MB service-worker precache and the 690KB idle bank prefetch: they buy the excellent mode-entry numbers above, and they are charged to every visitor on every first visit whether they play a quiz or not.

HOW TO THINK GOING FORWARD. Three rules, each of them earned by something that went wrong in this run. First: a developer machine cannot see this class of defect. The dead-tap window is 63ms unthrottled and 2,376ms at 4x CPU on slow 4G — the same bug, a 38x difference. Every perf claim in this repo should carry the throttle settings it was measured under, or it means nothing. Second: measure the frame, not the metric. FCP said 604ms and it was true and it was useless, because what painted was a decoy. The filmstrip and the tap test found what the timing API could not. Third — and this is the one that pays compound interest — we are guessing. CrUX has no data for balliq.app, so there is not one real-user speed measurement anywhere in this product, while /_vercel/speed-insights/script.js has been quietly loading on production the whole time. Read it. Alex asked to follow the data; right now this area is following a model of a phone. And when the dead-tap fix ships, measure it against onboard-done-answered vs onboard-done-skipped in funnel_events — that instrument went live 2026-08-22 and has 32 hours of data, so a before/after is available for free in about a week.

five_star_path:
WHAT GETS US TO 5 STARS HERE. Nothing on a product page earns a star; this area decides who ever gets the chance to give one. Two things do that: the assets must not look broken, and the page must show that other people already liked it. We fail both today. A visitor with ten seconds currently sees a hero image with a flame punched through the word "Daily", and — if they came from our own homepage — a page that says in plain English "This app hasn't received enough ratings or reviews to display an overview." Fix those two and the same listing converts materially better with no new content. Then close the review loop: SKStoreReviewController gives stars, and we have 8 of them and ZERO written sentences across six storefronts. Ratings are the ASO ranking input AND the trust signal, and we are collecting the cheap half of them. The specific ask that changes this: after a genuinely good moment (a 7/7 Daily, a 5-club Trail solve, a 10-day streak), and only for players src/lib/review.js already considers eligible, add one honest line — "If Ball IQ has been good, a sentence on the App Store is worth more to it than a star." Then send them to a country-correct write-review URL. Twenty written reviews at 4.9 with real football-fan language would do more for the install decision than any redesign in this report.

WHAT IMPROVES THE PRODUCT NOW. In rough order of cost-to-value, all verifiable in an afternoon: (1) Re-shoot all eight — the capture fix is already in scripts/shoot-store-screens.mjs:486, it just was not run over the set — and upload the phone set to Play TODAY, which needs no release. Carry the same eight into the 1.7.0 iOS submission. (2) Point every store CTA at balliq.app/get: src/lib/links.js:21-28, its six call sites, and the two hardcoded country-less links in scripts/seo/content.mjs:34 and scripts/gen-seo-pages.mjs:5649. Add eg, ng, jp, kr to the allow-list in both files while you are there. (3) Fix the two caption overclaims in scripts/frame-store-screens.mjs — line 97's "THE ULTIMATE FOOTBALL QUIZ" (the phrase we deliberately deleted from the description, still live in the picture and in balliq.app's <title>) and lines 122-124's "every time" against a measured 84.3%. (4) Reorder: the explanation shot to slot 2, the club list out of the top three, Trail seeded to solve on 2 clubs not 5, Daily 7 seeded to 7/7. (5) Re-shoot the Mystery shot against the 1.7.0 ranking so we stop advertising Buffon at 1,689. (6) The icon is the one thing here worth real money: a mark built from our own black/green/gold that survives at 60px and is not the fifth flaming football on the shelf.

HOW TO THINK GOING FORWARD. Three principles, each earned from something I found today. First: the store assets are a SECOND IMPLEMENTATION of every claim the app makes, and they drift silently. Every one of the four description corrections landed; not one of the equivalent screenshot captions did. When a claim gets corrected, grep the captions. Better — generate the screenshot copy from the same source of truth as the listing copy, so the "every answer / most answers" split cannot happen twice. Second: a store asset check must assert what the image LOOKS like, not which screen it is. The old verify tested txt.includes(s.expect) and passed a visibly broken PNG for eight days; forceOpaqueMaterials is the right fix and it returns the list it repaired — make a non-empty return FAIL the shoot rather than log, and make the shoot refuse to emit a partial set, because a one-of-eight fix pack is how screenshot 6 survived. Third, and this is the honest strategic answer to "big strides, brick by brick": the listing craft here is already well above the indie median — the copy is specific and honest, the keyword hygiene is deliberate, fifteen locales are live, /get is correct and deployed. Polishing it further has a low ceiling while we are absent from 156 results for the phrase in our own name and have eight ratings. The bricks that matter for this area, in order, are: stop shipping broken images, stop sending people to the empty shelf, and turn 500 downloads and a 4.88 average into twenty written reviews. Discovery follows ratings; it does not lead them.

five_star_path:
Alex asked three things. Answering each for this area.

**"What gets us to 5 stars?"** — In this category people do not give 5 stars for stability; they take stars AWAY for it. The specific removals are: a crash they saw, a run they lost, and an app that feels like it forgot them. We are exposed on the middle one and I proved it by losing my own run on production. So the 5-star path here is three fixes, in this order:
1. **Persist the in-flight run** (localStorage snapshot per question, cleared on completion). This is the only finding in my area I personally experienced as a player, and "I lost my run" is the most common 1-star sentence in quiz apps. Footle and Trail already prove the pattern exists in this codebase.
2. **Wrap the core loop in TabErrorBoundary** — quiz x3, results x3, Footle, Club Quiz, League Quiz. The component and its `onExit` variant are already written; this is copy-paste. It converts "the whole app died" into "this screen hit a snag, here's Home", which is the difference between a 1-star and no review at all.
3. **Make the root boundary mark a bad review moment.** One line. Today the worst crash in the app leaves the rating ask armed. That is actively converting our crashes into 1-star ratings instead of silence.

**"What should we improve now?"** — The release process, not the code. The code passed everything I ran: eslint 0, 234/234 tests, 5 audits, Sentry verified transmitting, SW verified complete, boot watchdogs verified present inside the actual .app. What failed is the safety net around shipping. `npm run verify:native` printed a green tick over a bundle three commits stale. Add two greps to scripts/prune-native-web-assets.mjs and hard-fail: (a) the `assets/index-*.js` name in `ios/App/App/public/index.html` must equal the one in `dist/index.html`; (b) the `release:"…"` string in that bundle must equal `git rev-parse --short HEAD`. That second check also catches the mistagged-release bug for free. Then add `dist:` to Sentry.init so build 75 and build 76 are distinguishable.

**"How should we think going forward?"** — Two shifts. First: **the guard has to fail before you trust it.** Six detectors in this repo were wrong on their first run; `verify:native` makes seven, and my own boundary-coverage script made two errors in thirty rows before I hand-checked it. Never add a check without breaking it on purpose once. Second: **at 500 installs, native has no undo.** Web can be fixed in four minutes; a bad native build is live for two days with no lever. That asymmetry should change how the release feels — everything that can be a remote switch (a mode toggle, a minimum version, a message) should be, so the store review stops being the only lever we have.

**Would I upload 1.7.0 today?** Yes on substance — nothing I found is a reason to hold it, and the 1.6.0 users are missing a week of real fixes. But not by pressing Archive on the current working tree. In order: (1) `rm -rf dist && npm run build` from a clean HEAD; (2) `npm run sync:ios && npm run sync:android`; (3) grep `release:"…"` in `ios/App/App/public/assets/index-*.js` and confirm it equals HEAD — this is the check that does not exist yet and is the whole reason build 75 shipped mistagged; (4) put it on Alex's real phone and search a player in Trail, then drag the list — the keyboard fix is the entire point of 75/76 and no browser and no simulator can answer it (I did rule out the commit's own stated suspect: CapacitorKeyboard.framework and KeyboardPlugin ARE in the built app); (5) `npm run ratings` per storefront before and after, because GB at 3 ratings is the shelf that matters and an aggregate would hide it.

WHAT GETS US TO 5 STARS. Read the two rivals' listings honestly: the 1.1k-rating leader is free-with-ads plus £2.99/£4.99 IAP, and its own reviewers dock it for ads and for rejecting correct typed answers. The 25,000-question rival paywalls its clubs at £6.99 and ships no explanations. Our differentiator is not size, it is that we are the only one in the set that never interrupts, never charges, and tells you WHY. So the five-star path is not new features — it is making that true everywhere and making it visible at the moment of judgement. Three things, in order. (1) Fix Play Again on club and league quizzes. It is one line, it is live on all three surfaces right now, and it is the moment a player who just fell in love with their club's pack gets handed someone else's. (2) Close the explanation gap where it is actually seen: 217 unexplained World Cup 2026 questions and 386 unexplained easy ones, before the tournament, using the forge that already produced 89-for-89 on summer2026. "Most answers come with a short explanation" should become "every answer" and then be said out loud. (3) Fix the repeat floor on the ten packs under 20 questions — a supporter of a small club is our most likely reviewer and currently gets the same ten questions twice.

WHAT IMPROVES THE PRODUCT NOW. The prod numbers say the portfolio is the product: players who touched one mode averaged 1.09 active days, four modes 5.73, six modes 8.38, nine modes 19.0. Footle and Daily 7 are the only surfaces above two days per player. So stop treating breadth as a feature list and start treating it as the retention mechanism — put all four dailies in the Home DAILY block instead of two, and resolve True/False either into a real entry point or into the bin. Then use the moat where it is idle: 86 club packs earn 75 plays a month in-app while the same content carries the entire SEO strategy. A club a player picks once should stick — one tap back into that club from the results screen, a per-club best score, a per-club board. That is the same fix as (1) above viewed from the other end, and it costs nothing new.

HOW TO THINK GOING FORWARD. Brick by brick, following the data, means this: we are not competing on question count and we should never print one — Legends claims 25,000 and locks nine clubs behind £6.99. We compete on the four things I verified we uniquely have: four dailies in one app with a history grid, an explanation on the answer, sixteen countries of clubs including the ones nobody else bothers with, and no ads and no paywall anywhere. Every one of those is currently under-delivered at the last step rather than missing — the picker is beautiful and stuck on web, the explanations exist and skip the World Cup, the dailies are four and shown as two, the moat is deep and re-entry drops it. The discipline for the next quarter is to stop adding differentiators and finish the four we have, then say them plainly on the GB shelf where three ratings decide whether anyone installs. Two deliberate NOTs: do not copy ads or a club paywall, because "free and uninterrupted" is the only claim in this category we can make that the market leader cannot; and do not chase the guess-the-XI clone on its own terms — if /lineup ever ships, it ships as QUIZ THE XI, which needs our bank and therefore cannot be cloned back.
